title: Grateful Dead Live at Berkeley Community Theatre on 1972-08-22
lineage: Set 1: Master Dat (Sony R500) -> Behringer UltraMatch SRC 2000 -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> Cool Edit Pro v2.0 -> SHN. Set 2 : CD -> EAC -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> SHN
source: Set 1 : SBD -> Master Reel (10 inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> Apogee AD500 -> Master Dat (Panasonic SV3800/48k).  Set 2 : SBD -> Master Reel (10 inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> PCM -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: Superb soundboard capture of a scorching August ’72 Berkeley set featuring a rare slide‑driven Hey Bo Diddley, an epic Other One and crystal‑clear vocals.
ai_review.review: The Miller transfer delivers an excellent two‑track off‑the‑board mix that is crisp, balanced and virtually free of major glitches. Musically the band is on fire – Jerry’s dizzying licks, Keith’s vibey keys and Phil’s thunderous bass solo on The Other One lift a mellow first set into a high‑energy second set highlighted by a rare Hey Bo Diddley segue into Not Fade Away.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews (9 out of 11) rate the show 4–5 stars and praise both performance and recording; technical notes are uniformly positive, giving a strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear two‑track off‑the‑board mix with Miller's superb remaster; reviewers note crisp vocals and instruments, minor glitches mentioned but not detracting from overall listenability.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts mellow, builds into a high‑octane second set; rare slide‑driven Hey Bo Diddley bridges into Not Fade Away, with the Other One serving as an epic centerpiece.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as ripping dizzying fluttering licks and delivering a squeaking white Strat that drives the band forward.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for being on top of his game, laying a groove foundation and delivering an impressive bass solo/workout in The Other One.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for a solid groove‑laced foundation and engaging Gibson counter‑punching against Jerry's lead.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith joins the vibe early, adding to the rising intensity; the venue’s acoustics let the keyboards shine.
